The CloudTalk REST API gives you programmatic access to your call center data and operations. It is organized around resources, such as AI Voice Agents, Contacts, Calls and Webhooks, with predictable, resource-oriented URLs. All requests are made over HTTPS, and responses are UTF-8 encoded JSON.

## [​](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/overview\#api-hosts)  API hosts

The API is served from four hosts. Each endpoint page shows its full URL.

| Host | What’s there | Style |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `https://api.cloudtalk.io/v1` | AI Voice Agents, AI Conversation Intelligence, Contacts, AI Sales Dialer & Campaigns, Call tags, User status, Webhooks | Current API: standard HTTP methods, JSON bodies, cursor pagination, and errors with a stable code. The AI Sales Dialer and AI Conversation Intelligence keep response and error shapes of their own. |
| `https://my.cloudtalk.io/api` | Calls, Messaging (SMS & WhatsApp), Numbers, Agents, Groups, Utilities, and the legacy Contacts, Contact tags, Bulks and Campaigns endpoints | Classic API: `.json` paths, a `responseData` envelope, `PUT` creates and `POST` updates, page-based pagination. |
| `https://analytics-api.cloudtalk.io/api` | Call flow analytics: [Get call details](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/calls/get-call-details), the one Calls endpoint on this host | Its own shape: a bare JSON object, no `responseData` envelope. |
| `https://platform-api.cloudtalk.io/api` | [CueCard](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/cuecard/create-cuecard) | Its own shape: `{ success, errors }`. |

The same API key works on every host, and a request sent to the wrong host answers `404`. For new integrations, use the v1 endpoints where they exist: the v1 Contacts endpoints rather than the legacy ones, and the AI Sales Dialer endpoints for campaigns.

## [​](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/overview\#authentication)  Authentication

Every request to the CloudTalk API must include HTTP Basic Auth credentials — the same key pair on every host. Use your **API Access Key ID** as the username and your **API Access Key Secret** as the password.

```
curl -u YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET \
  https://my.cloudtalk.io/api/calls/index.json
```

Only Administrators can create API keys. You can generate and manage them in the CloudTalk Dashboard under **Settings → API Keys** ( [open directly](https://dashboard.cloudtalk.io/menu/account/settings/API-keys)).

Keep your API credentials secure. Do not commit them to source control or expose them in client-side code. Rotate your credentials immediately if they are compromised.

## [​](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/overview\#response-envelope)  Response Envelope

All successful responses from the classic API are wrapped in a top-level `responseData` object. Paginated collection endpoints include pagination metadata alongside the `data` array.

```
{
  "responseData": {
    "itemsCount": 100,
    "pageCount": 2,
    "pageNumber": 1,
    "limit": 50,
    "data": [ ... ]
  }
}
```

Single-resource responses omit the pagination fields and return the resource object directly inside `responseData`.

```
{
  "responseData": {
    "id": "42",
    "status": "answered",
    ...
  }
}
```

The current API has no `responseData` envelope. It returns one resource as a
bare object and a list as `{ data, pagination: { limit, next }, requestId }`;
AI Sales Dialer lists are `{ data, meta }`. [Response\\
envelopes](https://help.cloudtalk.io/guides/response-envelopes) shows every shape.

## [​](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/overview\#http-methods)  HTTP Methods

**The classic API does not use `POST` and `PUT` the way most REST APIs do.** On
`my.cloudtalk.io/api`, **`PUT` creates** and **`POST` updates**, the reverse of
the usual convention. Reaching for `POST` to create a resource there will not work.

| Method | Current API (`api.cloudtalk.io/v1`) | Classic API (`my.cloudtalk.io/api`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | Read a resource or list a collection. Never modifies data. | Read a resource or list a collection. Never modifies data. |
| `POST` | Create a resource or trigger an action. | **Update** a resource, for example `POST /agents/edit/{agentId}.json`. |
| `PUT` | Replace a resource or a sub-collection, for example [Replace a voice agent](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/voiceagent/replace-a-voice-agent) or [Set a user’s status](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/user-status/set-a-users-status). | **Create** a resource, for example `PUT /agents/add.json`. |
| `PATCH` | Update part of a resource, for example [Update a contact](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/contacts/update-a-contact). | Not used. |
| `DELETE` | Delete a resource. | Delete a resource. |

Three classic endpoints are actions rather than updates, and use `POST` for that:
[Make a call](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/calls/make-a-call), [Send\\
sms](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/sms/send-sms) and the legacy [Contact\\
actions](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/bulks-legacy/contact-actions). Not every current surface
offers every method: AI Conversation Intelligence is read-only, for example.

## [​](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/overview\#error-handling)  Error Handling

When a request fails, CloudTalk returns an appropriate HTTP status code along with a JSON body describing the error. On the classic API, the body is wrapped in `responseData`:

```
{
  "responseData": {
    "status": 404,
    "message": "Call not found"
  }
}
```

On the current API, errors are `{ error: { code, message, target, details }, requestId }`,
with the codes listed on each endpoint page; the AI Sales Dialer and AI
Conversation Intelligence use `{ statusCode, message, error, correlationId }`,
and starting or stopping AI voice agent calls answers `application/problem+json`.
[Error codes](https://help.cloudtalk.io/guides/error-codes) lists every shape.Common status codes you will encounter across all endpoints:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Success |
| `400` | Bad request — malformed parameters |
| `401` | Unauthorized — missing or invalid credentials |
| `403` | Forbidden — action not permitted for this account |
| `404` | Not found — resource does not exist |
| `406` | Not acceptable — invalid input value |
| `409` | Conflict — resource state prevents this action |
| `410` | Gone — resource existed but has been permanently deleted |
| `429` | Too many requests — rate limit exceeded |
| `500` | Internal server error |

## [​](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/overview\#pagination)  Pagination

Classic API collection endpoints support pagination via `limit` and `page` query parameters. The response envelope includes `itemsCount`, `pageCount`, and `pageNumber` fields to help you iterate through large result sets.

```
# Fetch page 2 with 100 items per page
curl -u YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET \
  'https://my.cloudtalk.io/api/calls/index.json?limit=100&page=2'
```

The maximum value for `limit` is `1000` on the classic API.The current API pages with a cursor instead: pass `limit`, then send the
`pagination.next` of each answer back as `cursor` until it is `null` (on the AI
Sales Dialer, `meta.nextCursor`). See [Pagination](https://help.cloudtalk.io/guides/pagination).

## [​](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/overview\#resources)  Resources

The API is divided into the following resource groups, in the order of the sidebar:

[**AI Voice Agents** \\
\\
Create and manage AI voice agents and their knowledge bases, start outbound AI calls, and stop outbound dialing in an emergency.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/voiceagent/initiate-voiceagent-call)

[**AI Conversation Intelligence** \\
\\
Read the AI analysis of a call: summary, transcription, sentiment, topics, talk-listen ratio and smart notes.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/conversation-intelligence/summary)

[**Contacts** \\
\\
Search, create, update and delete contacts, upsert up to 100 at a time, and manage contact tags and contact fields.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/contacts/list-and-search-contacts)

[**AI Sales Dialer & Campaigns** \\
\\
Manage AI Sales Dialer campaigns, campaign contacts, call scripts, surveys, disposition buttons, statistics and exports.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/dialer/list-dialer-campaigns)

[**Calls** \\
\\
Access call history, download recordings, start outbound calls, and read real-time group statistics.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/calls/call-history)

[**Call tags** \\
\\
List the plain call tags, read a call’s tags, and add or remove them.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/call-tags/list-call-tags)

[**Messaging** \\
\\
Send SMS and WhatsApp messages from your CloudTalk numbers, one recipient per request.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/sms/send-sms)

[**Numbers** \\
\\
List and configure the phone numbers assigned to your CloudTalk account.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/numbers/list-numbers)

[**User status** \\
\\
Read what each user is doing now, set a user Online or Idle, and list the status types.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/user-status/list-user-statuses)

[**Agents** \\
\\
List, add, edit and delete the agents in your account.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/agents/list-agents)

[**Groups** \\
\\
List agent groups, and add an agent to a group or remove one.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/groups/list-groups)

[**Webhooks** \\
\\
Manage webhook endpoints, their signing secrets, test events and the delivery log.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/webhooks/list-webhook-event-types)

[**Utilities** \\
\\
Read supporting data such as the countries list, and manage the inbound call blacklist.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/utilities/list-countries)

[**CueCard** \\
\\
Show real-time guidance cards to agents during live calls.](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/cuecard/create-cuecard)

## [​](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/overview\#legacy)  Legacy

These older endpoints on `my.cloudtalk.io/api` keep working unchanged. Use
their replacements for new integrations:

- [Contacts (LEGACY)](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/contacts-legacy/list-contacts): use
[Contacts](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/contacts/list-and-search-contacts). Notes and
activities have no v1 equivalent yet.
- [Contact tags (LEGACY)](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/contact-tags-legacy/list-contact-tags):
use [Contact tags](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/contacts/list-contact-tags).
- [Bulks (LEGACY)](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/bulks-legacy/contact-actions): use [Bulk\\
upsert contacts](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/contacts/bulk-upsert-contacts) to create and
update up to 100 contacts. Bulk delete has no v1 equivalent yet: delete one
contact at a time with [Delete a contact](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/contacts/delete-a-contact).
- [Campaigns (LEGACY)](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/campaigns-legacy/list-campaigns): use the
[AI Sales Dialer campaign endpoints](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/dialer/list-dialer-campaigns).

## [​](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/overview\#rate-limits)  Rate Limits

CloudTalk enforces rate limits to ensure platform stability. If you exceed the allowed request rate, the API returns a `429 Too Many Requests` response. Implement exponential backoff in your integration to handle transient rate-limit errors gracefully.

For high-volume integrations, batch contact writes with [Bulk upsert contacts](https://help.cloudtalk.io/api-reference/contacts/bulk-upsert-contacts) (up to 100 contacts per request), and cache reference data (agents, groups, tags) locally rather than fetching it on every request.
